sources.readDepth: Targeted controls, specificity/gating, sequential-gating and tissue-resident T-cell data-analysis passages, not the whole 438-page guideline.
verifiedClauses: FMO stains all selected labels except one to help identify gating boundaries.
FMO does not account for every nonspecific antibody-binding shift; biological controls address another question.
Single-stain compensation controls and gating controls have different jobs.
Sequential gating names parent populations and can exclude unexpected or rare subsets.
The stated T-cell example uses good-flow time regions, lymphocytes, singlets, compensation and viable CD3-positive cells before CD4/CD8 subdivision.
limits: No one mandatory gate order for all tissues and tasks is inferred.
Sorting definition and the other remaining lesson clauses still require their own source/field mapping.
sources.reviewGapResolved: R5 FMO/gating source availability; R7 gating content can now be authored with stated example scope.

sources.identity: Statistical Guidance on Reporting Results from Studies Evaluating Diagnostic Tests, issued 13 March 2007.
sources.readDepth: Section 7.1, printed page 21, and its intended-use/reference-standard discussion.
verifiedClauses: Sensitivity conditions on the presence of the condition of interest; specificity conditions on its absence.
Performance estimates use a reference standard and subjects representative of the intended-use population.
limits: Dated nonbinding guidance; generic performance terminology, not clinical validation of an oncology MRD assay.

sources.identity: FDA/CDRH/OIR Consult Review Memo, 7 November 2018, DDTBMQ000044, Plasmodium 18S rRNA/rDNA biomarker. The search display filename suggesting 2013 is not the document date.
sources.readDepth: Header/context and Appendix I terminology on printed page 23.
verifiedClauses: LoD is a conditional detection-concentration concept; the document describes typically 95 percent detection in a defined sample type.
LoQ is the lowest measurand amount determined with stated accuracy, expressed as total error or bias/precision criteria, under stated experimental conditions.
limits: This review concerns a malaria biomarker, not validation of cancer detection.
No universal 95 percent rule or interchangeability of detection and quantitative accuracy is adopted.
Definitions cited by FDA are not a claim that the full CLSI standard was read.
